payload.finding: A handover document was sent on 2026-06-12 containing full login credentials for the HostPeak hosting account and domain ownership, confirming the client now owned all accounts.

data.summary: The freelancer delivered a fully functional website on schedule, handed over all credentials, and the client used it successfully for months. The current error page is a HostPeak suspension caused by the client’s own billing lapse, not a failure of the freelancer’s delivery.

client_concerns.concern: We do not have a working website
client_concerns.answer: The freelancer launched the site on 2026-06-12 and it responded with HTTP 200, confirming a working website was delivered. A reversed payment would revert ownership of the site back to the freelancer, but the site itself was functional at launch.

client_concerns.concern: Patients searching for us get an error page
client_concerns.answer: The error page is an HTTP 503 "Account Suspended – HostPeak" generated when the client’s hosting account payment lapsed. The handover document explicitly warned the client to check the HostPeak payment method in such cases. If the payment is updated, the site returns to normal. A chargeback would not fix the hosting suspension.

client_concerns.concern: The service was never properly provided
client_concerns.answer: The proposal defined a 6‑page website with an appointment form, to be launched on the client’s own hosting account, and includes 30 days of post‑launch bug‑fix support. All deliverables were handed over on 2026‑06‑12. A reversed payment would undo the contractual transfer of ownership but would not change that the agreed‑upon service was delivered.

data.rationale: The freelancer delivered the agreed 6‑page website on 2026‑06‑12, confirmed by launch email and continuous uptime with HTTP 200 for over 100 days. The client acknowledged the live, functional site and even received appointment requests. The current error page is a HostPeak "Account Suspended" response caused by the client’s unpaid hosting bill, which the contract explicitly makes the client responsible for. The freelancer’s obligation for post‑launch bug‑fix support ended on 2026‑07‑12, so there is no contractual duty to fix hosting issues after that date. Because the service was delivered as contracted, the chargeback under MERCHANDISE_OR_SERVICE_NOT_RECEIVED is invalid. The real need is to reactivate the hosting account; the freelancer can resolve this by offering paid assistance to update the hosting payment or provide additional support at the agreed $80/hour rate, but no refund is owed.

proof_plan.point: Service was delivered and functional at launch on 2026‑06‑12
Client acknowledged receipt and that the site was working
Current error page is due to client’s hosting account suspension, not a delivery failure
Contract limited post‑launch support to 30 days; no obligation after 2026‑07‑12
Chargeback reason MERCHANDISE_OR_SERVICE_NOT_RECEIVED is unsupported because service was delivered

data.resolution_action: Offer to assist the client in reactivating the HostPeak hosting account (e.g., updating the payment method) and provide any further website support at the contract rate of $80/hour (or a discounted one‑time fee). No refund is required because the contracted service was delivered.
